- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at +1.5% above true for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits high volatility bias; smooth forecast by averaging last 3 values before adjustment.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; apply 1–3% downward bias for next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.
- For sentiment history with alternating 0.67/0.00, model tends to oscillate; use moving average of last 5 forecasts to dampen noise.
